facts: Adjusted EPS was $0.31 for Q4 2025 compared to $0.36 for Q4 2024, a decline of 13.9% year-over-year.
The company recorded $52.9 million of noncash impairment charges in Q4 2025, primarily related to combining the Abilene Truckload brand into the Swift business.
For full year 2025, the Truckload segment grew adjusted operating income by $28 million despite a $125 million decline in truckload revenue excluding fuel surcharge.
The Truckload business held 2025 cost per mile flat with 2024 despite miles declining 3.6%.
U.S. Xpress improved its adjusted operating ratio by 430 basis points year-over-year to the mid-90s in Q4 2025.
LTL revenue excluding fuel surcharge grew 7% year-over-year with shipments per day up 2.1% and door count growth of 10% year-over-year.
Management stated the existing LTL infrastructure has capacity to support annualized revenue of $2 billion.
The company projects Q1 2026 adjusted EPS in the range of $0.28 to $0.32.
Regulatory enforcement has put nearly 12,000 drivers out of service since June due to English proficiency requirements, with 17,000 non-domicile CDLs in California potentially expiring in March.
Truckload segment costs declined approximately $150 million in 2025, with roughly two-thirds from variable costs and one-third from fixed costs, and nondriver headcount was reduced by about 5%.

Q1 2026 total revenue was flat year-over-year while adjusted EBITDA rose 3.3% to $314 million and AFFO was $201 million or $0.78 per share, down 9.3% year-over-year primarily due to the expiration of prior year interest rate hedges.

Same-store physical occupancy declined 290 basis points sequentially to 76.4% (down only 30 bps year-over-year), with economic occupancy at 82%, and same-store NOI declined 0.9% to $347 million, all better than expectations.

Same-store rent, storage and blast revenue per physical pallet rose 2.2% year-over-year (fourth consecutive quarterly increase), with Q1 same-store NOI benefiting roughly 250 basis points from favorable FX, expected to moderate to ~100 bps in Q2.

Container volumes declined 17% year-over-year in Q1 following a 9% decline in Q4 2025, contributing to a 3.3% drop in throughput volumes, though services revenue per throughput pallet still rose 50 bps.

Management reiterated full-year 2026 guidance of same-store NOI of -4% to -1%, adjusted EBITDA of $1.25B–$1.30B, and AFFO of $2.75–$3.00 per share, while expressing increased conviction in hitting the midpoint.

Lineage invested $130 million of growth capital in Q1 and has $1.2 billion deployed across 22 facilities under construction or ramping, expected to add over $150 million of incremental EBITDA at stabilization.
The company has secured 70% of its 2026 rate increases, supporting confidence in delivering 1%–2% net price increases across the warehousing portfolio for the year.

Approximately 85% of U.S. NOI sits in markets with low or already-digested new supply, while ~15% remains pressured by late-cycle supply delivered in 2024–2025; industry-wide new supply deliveries are expected to slow below 2% in 2026 and 2027.

A $50 million-plus administrative cost reduction plan is underway, with roughly half realized in 2026 and full benefit in 2027, requiring ~$15 million of upfront investment booked below EBITDA; quarterly admin expense is expected to normalize to $120–$125 million for the rest of 2026.

Lineage ended Q1 with $7.9 billion of net debt and $1.6 billion of liquidity, reported leverage of 6.0x (adjusted 5.3x) versus a 5.0–5.5x target, with ~$600 million of 2026 debt maturities and a strategic portfolio review underway exploring asset sales, JVs and larger transactions, none of which would be dilutive.
Q3 2025 revenue grew 39% year-over-year to $265.2 million, and the company crossed over $1 billion in annualized revenue for the first time.
Oncology test volumes increased 40% year-over-year to approximately 74,000 tests in Q3, with Guardant360 Liquid delivering its fifth consecutive quarter of accelerating growth at more than 30%.
Excluding the screening business, Guardant generated positive free cash flow during Q3, achieving this milestone one quarter ahead of the stated target.
Shield screening revenue totaled $24.1 million from approximately 24,000 tests, with ASP of approximately $880 and non-GAAP gross margin improving from negative at launch to 55% in Q3.
Reveal COGS declined from over $1,000 per test in Q3 2024 to less than $500 per test, contributing to non-GAAP gross margin improvement to 66% from 63% in the prior year period.
Full-year 2025 revenue guidance was raised for the third time to $965 million to $970 million, representing approximately 31% growth compared to 2024.
Shield revenue guidance was increased to $71 million to $73 million from $55 million to $60 million, with volume expectations raised to 80,000-82,000 tests from 68,000-73,000 tests.
The company ended Q3 with approximately $690 million in cash, cash equivalents, and restricted cash, with free cash flow burn improving by $9.5 million year-over-year to $45.8 million.

The Quest Diagnostics partnership provides immediate connectivity to 650,000 clinician and hospital accounts, access to 2,000 patient service centers, and 6,000 in-office phlebotomists in the United States.
Guardant now has 23 total CDx approvals across biomarker and tumor types, including two new companion diagnostic approvals in Q3 for breast cancer and non-small cell lung cancer indications.
Fiscal 2025 full year diluted EPS was $1.92 compared with $1.90 in the prior year, while fiscal 2026 diluted EPS guidance is $1.98 to $2.18.

Full year fiscal 2025 sales grew 5.1% to $4.684 billion with comparable store sales declining 1.8%, while fiscal 2026 sales guidance is $4.880 billion to $5.03 billion with comps estimated at down 2% to up 1%.
China represented only 3% of fourth quarter receipts, down from 12.5% in the prior year period, reflecting meaningful progress in diversifying product sourcing.

January 2026 comparable store sales increased 0.4%, marking the first January increase since 2022, but winter storm Fern disrupted operations across more than 55% of stores, contributing 200 to 300 basis points of quarter-to-date comp pressure or $12 million to $18 million in lost sales.

New store capital expenditure per store for the class of 2026 is expected to be approximately $7 million to $8 million, down from $10.2 million for the class of 2025, which itself was $1.2 million or 11% lower than the fiscal 2023 class.
Spartan Surfaces fiscal 2025 sales increased approximately 13% to $243 million, surpassing expectations and reinforcing the strength of the commercial platform.
Fiscal 2026 adjusted EBITDA is expected to be approximately $560 million to $590 million, with the 53rd week contributing approximately $11 million.
Over the last 3 years, the company has taken almost $67 million out of comparable store costs, including approximately $24.8 million in fiscal 2025, while achieving record Net Promoter Scores.
Stores greater than 5 years old are generating approximately $21 million in sales and 23% EBITDA margins, while only 30% of the fleet is currently operating on minimum hours.

Full year gross margin expanded 30 basis points to 43.6%, with distribution center investments in Seattle and Baltimore creating approximately 70 basis points of gross margin pressure, offset by favorable product margins from lower supply chain costs.
Nautilus ended Q1 2026 with $143.4 million in cash, cash equivalents and investments, with management reiterating cash runway extends through 2027.
Q1 2026 cash burn was $12.8 million, benefiting from lower spend and $1.1 million in cash generated from stock option exercises.
Total Q1 2026 operating expenses fell 14% year-over-year to $16.1 million, with R&D down 16% to $9.7 million and G&A down 12% to $6.4 million.

Full-year 2026 revenue guidance remains approximately $0.5 million, though Michael J. Fox Foundation grant revenue recognition has shifted to later quarters due to Middle East conflict-related delays.
Commercial launch is still planned for late 2026 via preorders, with customer instrument installations beginning early 2027 and broadscale general availability in the first half of 2027.
Nautilus built out its commercial team in Q1, hiring VP of Global Sales Amber Faust roughly two months ago plus two additional sales reps, forming a three-person sales organization.
Baylor College of Medicine was announced as the first named Iterative Mapping Early Access Program customer, with its first official samples to be processed shortly.
The Tau service lab passed formal verification and validation, meeting requirements for accuracy, dynamic range, reproducibility and stability.
Nautilus nearly tripled the number of affinity reagent probes qualified as assay-compatible in Q1, driven by newer assay configurations for the broadscale platform.

The company narrowed its oncology proteoform target list to priority candidates including EGFR, AKT1 and p53, with one oncology-focused proteoform assay on track to enter early access in the second half of 2026.
Adjusted EBITDA margin improved to negative 1%, a 13 percentage point improvement year-over-year, representing the company's best margin as a public company.
The Board authorized a new $12 million share repurchase program following strong financial performance.
The company expects to generate positive adjusted EBITDA in Q4 2025 and for full year 2026, assuming low single-digit revenue growth.
Cost savings totaling $7 million annually were achieved through net headcount reduction, performance marketing efficiencies, and other measures.
GMV accelerated to up 5% in Q3 compared to down 2% in Q2, driven by conversion growth and AOV rebound.
Q4 2025 guidance includes GMV of $90 million to $96 million, net revenue of $22.3 million to $23.5 million, and adjusted EBITDA margin of positive 2% to positive 5%.
On-platform average order value of nearly $2,700 and median order value of approximately $1,300 were both up 10% year-over-year.
Over 75% of traffic came from organic sources, up 3 percentage points year-over-year, reducing dependence on performance marketing.
The company ended Q3 with cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments of $93 million.
Over 25% of all new code is being written by AI, accelerating the development process as part of the company's efficiency initiatives.
Q1 2026 total revenue was approximately $840 million with adjusted EBITDA of approximately $181 million and adjusted EPS from continuing operations of $2.16.

Commercial Foodservice generated Q1 revenue of approximately $616 million with organic growth of 8.1% and organic adjusted EBITDA margins of 25.8%, while Food Processing delivered $224 million in revenue with 25% organic growth and 19.5% EBITDA margins.
Food Processing posted record Q1 orders of $231 million and a growing backlog of $416 million, marking its fifth consecutive quarter of book-to-bill above 1.

Middleby plans to spin off Food Processing into an independent public company, with RemainCo expected to have a net leverage ratio of approximately 2.8x at separation (delevering to 2.5x by year-end 2026) and the Food Processing SpinCo at approximately 1.25x.

The company repurchased 2.4 million shares (~5% of outstanding equity) for $366 million at ~$153.38/share in Q1, plus an additional 1.1 million shares for ~$154 million at ~$142/share early in Q2, totaling over $520 million YTD and ~7% share count reduction in 2026 (on top of 9% in 2025).
Full-year 2026 guidance was raised to revenue of $3.36B–$3.44B, adjusted EBITDA of $758M–$790M, and adjusted EPS of $9.54–$9.70.
Q2 2026 guidance calls for revenue of $815M–$850M, adjusted EBITDA of $180M–$192M, and adjusted EPS of $2.27–$2.39 on ~45.8 million weighted average shares.

Management announced low-single-digit price increases for Q3 to offset new inflationary pressures in shipping and electronic controls, estimating roughly a 1% margin headwind per segment from these costs.

Tariffs remained a margin headwind in Q1 and are expected to continue in Q2 before lapping prior-year pricing/mitigation actions in the second half, contributing to expected back-half margin improvement in Commercial Foodservice.

Management flagged increasingly strained consumer wallets in March and April with cautious guidance assumptions, but noted dealer/general market double-digit growth continued and chain replacement activity plus beverage menu expansion (including total beverage solutions) are driving upside expected to materialize meaningfully in 2027–2028.
AMG reported a 17% year-over-year increase in adjusted EBITDA and 27% growth in economic earnings per share in Q3 2025.
Firm-wide net inflows reached $9 billion in Q3 2025, bringing year-to-date total net inflows to $17 billion, representing a 3% annualized organic growth rate.
AMG added approximately $76 billion in alternative assets under management year-to-date, representing a nearly 30% increase in total alternative AUM.
Alternative strategies now contribute 55% of AMG's EBITDA on a run rate basis, with affiliates managing $353 billion in alternative AUM.
AMG posted $14 billion in net inflows in liquid alternatives in Q3 2025, the strongest quarterly net flows in liquid alternatives in the company's history.
The sale of AMG's minority stake in Comvest generated nearly 3x the original purchase price, with expected proceeds of approximately $285 million.
AMG is guiding Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA to $325-$370 million, including net performance fees of $75-$120 million, and economic earnings per share of $8.10-$9.26.
AMG has committed approximately $1.5 billion in capital across growth investments and share repurchases year-to-date in 2025, including more than $1 billion across 5 new growth investments.
AMG increased its full year 2025 share repurchase guidance to at least $500 million, up from approximately $350 million repurchased year-to-date.
AQR's assets grew from approximately $100 billion at the beginning of 2024 to $166 billion as of September 30, 2025, with most growth coming from organic flows.
U.S. cabozantinib franchise net product revenues grew approximately 14% year-over-year to $543 million in Q3 2025 compared to $478 million in Q3 2024.
Global cabozantinib franchise revenues were approximately $739 million in Q3 2025 compared to $653 million in Q3 2024.
CABOMETYX has achieved greater than 40% new patient share in the oral second-line plus neuroendocrine tumor segment.
Cabozantinib demand in neuroendocrine tumors grew approximately 50% quarter-over-quarter and contributed approximately 6% of Q3 2025 business.
The company expects NET indication revenue to exceed $100 million in 2025.
The Board authorized an additional $750 million share repurchase program expiring at the end of 2026.
The company is lowering R&D expense guidance by $75 million to a range of $850 million to $900 million for full year 2025.
STELLAR-303 met one of its dual primary endpoints with a 20% reduction in risk of death (HR 0.80, p=0.0045) for zanzalintinib plus atezolizumab versus regorafenib in the ITT population.
Cash and marketable securities at quarter end were approximately $1.6 billion.
The company is narrowing full year 2025 total revenue guidance to $2.3 billion to $2.35 billion and net product revenue guidance to $2.1 billion to $2.15 billion.
Q3 2025 revenue totaled $935 million, a decrease of 9.9% versus Q3 of last year.

Reduced demand from the federal government and 3 top customers combined drove approximately 8% of the year-over-year revenue decline, with each of the 4 discrete impacts contributing roughly 2 percentage points.
The company recorded a noncash goodwill impairment totaling $102 million in the quarter due to declines in current and projected business performance.
A $70 million noncash tax valuation allowance was recorded due to a 3-year cumulative loss position.
Adjusted earnings per share was $0.18 compared to $0.21 in the prior year quarter.
For Q4 2025, the company expects revenue to decline 12% to 14%, including 8% of negative impact from discrete large customers and federal contractors.
Q4 2025 adjusted EBITDA margin is expected to be approximately 3%, representing a 120 basis point sequential increase.
The Education segment achieved a 90% fill rate overall in the quarter for the first time, while the telecom specialty within SET achieved double-digit growth.
Adjusted SG&A expenses decreased 9.7% year-over-year, reflecting momentum on structural and volume-related cost optimization efforts.
Management indicated that continued revenue and margin pressure is likely through at least the first half of 2026 due to residual impacts from federal contractor and large customer demand reductions.
Procore delivered Q4 FY2025 revenue of $349 million, up 15.6% year-over-year, exceeding the high end of guidance.
Full year FY2025 non-GAAP operating margin was 14%, representing 400 basis points of year-over-year expansion.

Full year free cash flow reached $215 million, representing 69% year-over-year growth and a 16% free cash flow margin, with Q4 being the strongest free cash flow quarter in company history at $90 million.
Current RPO grew 22% year-over-year and current deferred revenue grew 18% year-over-year in Q4.
The number of customers spending more than $1 million in ARR reached 115, representing 34% year-over-year growth, while $100,000-plus ARR customers now total more than 2,700.
Procore Pay ended the year with nearly 450 customers, representing more than 70% year-over-year growth.
For full year FY2026, Procore guided revenue between $1.489 billion and $1.494 billion (approximately 13% growth), non-GAAP operating margin of 17.5% to 18%, and free cash flow margin of 19%.
Six- and seven-figure deals grew 20% year-over-year in Q4, on top of a very strong prior-year Q4 performance.
Procore has approximately 66,000 unique active AI users and nearly 700 customers who have created thousands of agents on the platform.
Weighted average diluted share count grew less than 1% in Q4, and excluding a onetime former CEO equity transition charge, SBC would have been 16.6% of revenue versus the reported 23%.
CF Industries generated full year 2025 adjusted EBITDA of approximately $2.9 billion, with net earnings of approximately $1.5 billion or $8.97 per diluted share.

The company returned $1.7 billion to shareholders in 2025, including over $1.3 billion to repurchase 16.6 million shares, representing approximately 10% of outstanding shares at the beginning of the year.

The Yazoo City Complex is not expected to resume production until Q4 2026 at the earliest, resulting in an estimated full-year EBITDA impact of approximately $200 million, though the company expects business interruption insurance proceeds to offset most or all of the loss.
CF Industries expects its network to produce approximately 9.5 million tons of gross ammonia in 2026, down from 10.1 million tons (97% utilization rate) in 2025.

Capital expenditures in 2026 are expected to total approximately $1.3 billion on a consolidated basis, with CF Industries' portion at approximately $950 million, including $550 million for sustaining CapEx and $400 million for the Blue Point joint venture and common infrastructure.
The Blue Point project remains on budget at $3.7 billion total capital spend with approximately $500 million built in as contingency, and the plant is still expected to come online in 2029.
The carbon capture and sequestration unit at Donaldsonville is expected to sequester just under 1.5 million tons of CO2 in 2026, up from approximately 700,000 tons in 2025.

NOLA urea pricing stood at $450 per short ton at the time of the call, $100 higher than December 2025 levels, with management seeing room for further upside in North America during the first half of 2026.

The company recorded two Q4 2025 impairment charges totaling $76 million, including $51 million related to discontinuing the electrolyzer pilot project at Donaldsonville and $25 million related to the Yazoo City incident.
The company completed its $3 billion share repurchase program authorized in 2022 and commenced a new $2 billion program with approximately $1.7 billion remaining, expiring in December 2029.
Bioventus delivered 10% organic revenue growth in Q4 2025 with adjusted EBITDA margin expanding by approximately 490 basis points year-over-year to 23%.
Q4 2025 cash from operations reached a record of approximately $38 million, nearly doubling compared to Q4 of the prior year.
Full year 2025 cash flow from operations increased 92% year-over-year to nearly $75 million, achieving the company's goal of nearly doubling cash flow from operations.
The company plans to allocate approximately $13 million of incremental investment in 2026 towards four growth drivers: PNS, PRP, ultrasonics, and the international business.
PNS and PRP combined are expected to provide a minimum of 200 basis points of revenue growth in 2026 with further acceleration anticipated in 2027.
2026 net sales guidance is $600 million to $610 million, with adjusted EPS expected to range from $0.73 to $0.77, representing earnings growth outpacing revenue growth.
2026 cash from operations is projected to range between $82 million and $87 million, an increase of approximately 10% to 17% over 2025.
Net leverage ratio declined to below 2.5x at end of Q4 2025, with management confident it will fall well below 2x by end of 2026.
Pain Treatments revenue advanced 15% in Q4, with approximately $2 million or slightly more attributed to favorable distributor order timing dynamics.
Segment growth expectations for 2026 are: Surgical Solutions at double-digit growth, Pain Treatments at mid- to high-single-digit growth, and Restorative Therapies at low- to mid-single-digit growth.
Q3 2025 revenue was $533 million, representing 5% organic growth year-over-year but an 8% decline on a reported basis due to the deconsolidation of IV Solutions from the Otsuka ICU Medical JV.
Adjusted EBITDA increased 12% year-over-year to $106 million in Q3, and adjusted diluted EPS rose 28% to $2.03 compared to $1.59 in the prior year.
The company raised full-year 2025 EBITDA guidance to $395-$405 million from the prior range of $380-$390 million, and updated full-year adjusted EPS guidance to $7.35-$7.65 from $6.85-$7.15.
ICU Medical has repaid $273 million in debt principal year-to-date in 2025, and expects to reach 2.5x net debt to EBITDA leverage by year-end.
Adjusted gross margin improved to 41% in Q3, and excluding the 2 percentage point tariff impact, would have been 43%, within 2 percentage points of the company's 45% target.
The Consumables business achieved a record quarter with 8% reported growth (7% organic), representing the best sequential increase in absolute dollars since Q2 2024.
IV Systems grew 9% reported (8% organic) in Q3, driven by double-digit growth in LVP pumps and dedicated sets from new installations and strong census utilization.
Q3 tariff expense was $9 million (reducing gross margin by approximately 2 percentage points), and full-year 2025 tariff expense is expected to be approximately $25 million.

The company completed a refinancing on October 31 that increased Term Loan A by $190 million to pay down the higher-rate Term Loan B, expected to save approximately $2 million annually in interest expense.

The company ended Q3 with $1.3 billion of debt and $300 million of cash, and generated $28 million in free cash flow during the quarter despite a $10 million outflow from reducing accounts receivable purchase program utilization to zero.

Fiscal 2025 net revenue grew 9% to $1.99 billion, with adjusted comp store sales growth of 6%, adjusted operating income of $102.5 million (up 56% year-over-year), AOI margin expansion of 160 basis points to 5.2%, and adjusted EPS of $0.80 versus $0.52 in 2024.

Fourth quarter net revenue grew 15.1% to $503 million with adjusted comp store sales of 4.8%, adjusted operating income of $17.6 million (up from $3.2 million prior year), and adjusted EPS of $0.15 versus a loss of $0.04 per share last year.

First quarter-to-date comp store sales are running in the mid-single-digit range with sequential traffic acceleration from Q4, despite significant weather disruptions from winter storms affecting approximately 15% of the store fleet.
Managed care comp sales grew low double digits in 2025, with managed care reaching 42% of revenues, and the company targets 50% as a long-term North Star.

Fiscal 2026 guidance calls for net revenue of $2.03 billion to $2.09 billion, adjusted comp store sales growth of 3% to 6%, adjusted operating income of $107 million to $133 million (implying ~100 bps margin expansion), and adjusted EPS of $0.85 to $1.09.
The company repaid $101.3 million in long-term debt and convertible notes in fiscal 2025, ending the year with net debt to adjusted EBITDA of 1.1x and total liquidity of $332 million.

Frames priced above $99 increased from 20% of the assortment at the start of 2025 to 40% at year-end, with a target of approximately 60% by the end of 2026, and branded frame mix is expected to increase from approximately 40% to approximately 70% by year-end 2026.

Ray-Ban Meta AI smart glasses are in 300 stores with sell-through exceeding expectations and are expected to be available in all stores by the end of Q2 2026, generating among the highest transaction values across customer types with very high prescription lens and premium lens attachment rates.

The company expects to open 30 to 35 new stores and close 10 to 15 stores in 2026 for net new store growth of 20 to 25, with capital expenditures of $73 million to $78 million, and a new $50 million share repurchase authorization was approved.

The company's multiyear cost savings plan remains on track to realize approximately $10 million in annualized savings in 2026, as part of an approximately $20 million total cost-out initiative over multiple years.
Q3 sales grew 7.5% to $3 billion with comparable sales increasing just 0.3%, while restaurant level margin declined 100 basis points year-over-year to 24.5%.
Households with income below $100,000, representing about 40% of total sales, are dining out less often due to economic concerns.
The company now anticipates full year comparable sales to decline in the low single-digit range, with Q4 comps expected to decline in the low to mid-single-digit range.
Inflation is accelerating into the mid-single-digit range primarily due to tariffs and rising beef costs, and the company does not plan to fully offset this incremental inflation in the near term.
The company will roll off 2 points of pricing in early December and plans to take a slow and measured approach to pricing in 2026 rather than all at once.
Chipotle repurchased $687 million of stock in Q3 at an average price of $42.39, bringing year-to-date repurchases to a record $1.67 billion at an average price of $47.74.
The Board authorized an additional $500 million to the share repurchase program, leaving $652 million remaining at quarter end.
Marketing costs increased to 3% of sales in Q3, up approximately 90 basis points year-over-year, and are expected to remain around 3% for Q4 and the full year.
The company anticipates opening between 350 and 370 new restaurants in 2026, including 10 to 15 partner-operated restaurants internationally.
The 25- to 35-year-old age group, which represents about 25% of total sales and to which Chipotle over-indexes, has meaningfully pulled back spending.
Q4 2025 revenue was $33.6 million, an increase of 418% compared to the same period last year and 3.3% sequential growth compared to Q3.
The company guided Q1 2026 adjusted EBITDA loss to narrow to negative $12 million, representing more than $6 million of sequential improvement from Q4's negative $18.6 million.
Full year 2026 revenue outlook was raised to $190 million, which includes the addition of the EMD acquisition and is achievable without any additional acquisitions.
The company had $57.3 million of cash and cash equivalents as of January 31, 2026.
Two customers have expanded to almost $10 million of annual revenue each, with several additional agreements valued at more than $1 million also closed.
Cost of revenue improved to 76.5% in Q4 from 83.4% in the prior year period, driven by growth in higher-margin business lines and improved pricing.
Over 40% of Gloo 360 customers are already using Workday, which motivated the acquisition of EMD, a leading Workday Service Partner.
The company remains confident in achieving adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q4 2026 and expects to approach adjusted EBITDA profitability in Q3 2026.
Platform revenue totaled $20.1 million in Q4, an increase of $13.8 million from Q4 of last year, with 1.6% sequential growth, while Platform solutions revenue was $13.5 million, up 6% sequentially.
For Q1 2026, the company expects a weighted average share count of approximately 80 million shares and guided Q1 revenue of $36 million.

Franklin Resources reported $16.9 billion in long-term net inflows for Q2 fiscal 2026, with positive long-term net flows in every region and long-term inflows of $118 billion, up 28% quarter-over-quarter and 38% year-over-year excluding reinvested distributions.
Adjusted operating income was $475 million, up 8.5% quarter-over-quarter and 25.8% year-over-year, with AUM at $1.68 trillion and an institutional won-but-unfunded pipeline steady at $20.2 billion.

Alternatives fundraising reached $14.3 billion in the quarter (including $13.2 billion in private markets), bringing fiscal year-to-date private markets fundraising to $22.7 billion, and management now expects to exceed the $25–$30 billion annual target.

Fixed income net outflows were approximately $300 million, but excluding Western, fixed income generated $3.6 billion in positive net flows, marking the ninth consecutive positive quarter, while equities saw $4.7 billion of net outflows.

Canvas reached a record $22.9 billion in AUM (up 27% quarter-over-quarter, doubling over the past 12 months) with $5.3 billion of positive net flows, and tax-managed products including Canvas now total $110 billion.
ETF AUM hit a new high of $61.6 billion (up 67% year-over-year) with $4.5 billion of net inflows in the 18th consecutive positive quarter, and active ETFs now represent 45% of ETF AUM.

Q3 guidance: effective fee rate mid-to-high 37 bps, compensation $830 million (assuming $50 million performance fee at 55% payout), IS&T $155 million, occupancy $70 million, and G&A $210–$215 million including $23–$25 million in elevated fundraising expenses.

Full-year FY26 expenses are guided to be slightly above FY25 (about 1.5% higher), with investment management fee revenue expected to grow at least 6% year-over-year, implying Q4 margin in the high 29s and full-year margin in the 27s, on track to 30%+ margins later in 2027.

Alternatives AUM totals $283 billion with approximately 90% having potential to earn fees and about 80% currently fee-generating; alternative credit represents $96 billion with less than 10% software exposure.

Evergreen private markets products reached $8 billion across three $1B+ vehicles and are raising approximately $200 million per month, while Lexington's flagship secondaries fund is on track with no expected cannibalization and an update likely by fiscal year-end (September) or possibly July.
The Board approved a new $5 billion share repurchase authorization, with the company expecting about $3 billion of share repurchases in 2025.
Commercial HVAC in the Americas was up 30% in Q3, with the applied equipment business up 60% and data center sales up approximately 250%.
The company is eliminating approximately 3,000 indirect positions, with carryover cost savings expected to exceed $100 million in 2026.
Data center sales are on track to double from $500 million last year to $1 billion this year, with backlog entering 2026 projected to be up about 20% year-over-year.
Q3 adjusted EPS was $0.67, down 13% year-over-year, with full year adjusted EPS guidance revised to about $2.65.
CSA Residential sales were down 30% in Q3, driven by approximately 40% volume decline offset by double-digit regulatory mix-up and pricing.
Field inventory levels are expected to be down 30% versus last year by year-end, the lowest level since 2018.
European residential heat pump sales were up about 15% in Q3, with German heat pump sales up approximately 45%.
The company expects about $0.20 of adjusted EPS tailwind in 2026 from the combination of carryover restructuring benefits, lower tax rate, and share repurchases.
Free cash flow guidance for 2025 is approximately $2 billion, reflecting lower earnings and higher anticipated cash restructuring costs of about $150 million.
Q1 2026 net sales were $878 million, up 10.3% year-over-year, though excluding FX and SEM contribution, revenue grew 3.6%.
Adjusted EBITDA was $115 million with a 13.1% margin, up $12 million and 20 basis points year-over-year, while adjusted diluted EPS rose 37% to $1.29 from $0.94.
Fuel Systems sales were $549 million (up 12%) with a 9.3% adjusted operating margin, while Aftermarket sales were $329 million (up 7.5%) with a 17% adjusted operating margin.

PHINIA reiterated full-year 2026 guidance: revenue of $3.5–$3.7 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $485–$525 million (13.7%–14.3% margin), adjusted free cash flow of $200–$240 million, and a 30%–34% tax rate.
